errors.english: the Sangha monastic community must quickly offer assistance and guidance regarding punishments and the like
errors.why: The pupil is the one who must exert himself and help, so that the preceptor/teacher quickly obtains probation (parivāsa) etc. from the Saṅgha and is quickly released from it; the Saṅgha is the source, not the helper.

fix.find: the Sangha monastic community must quickly offer assistance and guidance regarding punishments and the like, so that the individual may quickly "take up" the remedy and "separate" from the fault.
fix.replace: the pupil must exert himself and help so that they quickly obtain probation and the like from the Sangha and are quickly released from it.

errors.english: If there is a fault of concealing a remaining offense (shispa) an offense requiring purification from the preceptor or the resident teacher
errors.why: lhag ma is saṅghāvaśeṣa (not 'shispa'), and the clause says the preceptor or teacher has a concealed saṅghāvaśeṣa offense, not an offense 'from' them.

errors.english: the resident monk should not merely ask questions
errors.why: The point is that toward the teacher the only difference is that asking (permission) is not required; otherwise he does the bowl, robe and other services as above.

note: Generally follows the Vinayasūtra commentary on nissaya duties, but the opening misassigns who helps the teacher through probation and mishandles saṅghāvaśeṣa.

errors.english: is also the (Pradhana) Fundamental Nature/Primary Matter; however, this is said to be utterly hollow and lacking inherent nature
errors.why: The quoted Sāṃkhya verse says that what enters the path of sight is utterly hollow and without essence; the English turns it into a claim that the visible is the Pradhāna.

note: The argument against the Sāṃkhya pradhāna (manifest vs. capacity, hollowness transferring by non-difference) is followed correctly.

errors.english: The King uttered a cry of praise.
errors.why: It is the sky-going gods' cry of 'Well done, O King!' (nṛpa sādhuvāde) spreading to the ends of the directions, not the king praising.

fix.find: The King uttered a cry of praise.
fix.replace: As the gods' cry of "Well done, O King!" spread to the ends of the directions,

errors.english: With some wielding axes, though their hearts were moist with compassion
errors.why: The tree (the king) is moist with compassion (dayārdra); the woodcutters are the wicked, self-seeking ones.

fix.find: With some wielding axes, though their hearts were moist with compassion, this shady tree—straight,
fix.replace: By some wielding axes, this shady tree—moist with compassion, straight,

errors.english: began to speak of the unreal nature of things
errors.why: The grief-stricken people burst into distraught, baseless imaginings (abhūtārtha-vikalpa-jalpa), not a discourse on the unreality of things.

errors.english: This lovely tree, like a (sahakara) mango tree, cuts its own fragrant body.
errors.why: His fragrant body has been cut (chinna-tanu), so he has become a true mango tree; he is not cutting himself.

note: Gets the gist of the lament but misattributes the praise and the compassion in the opening verses.

errors.english: bypasses the customs process without attachment
errors.why: ma chags pa here means the duty is not incurred or levied, not 'without attachment'.

errors.english: If the carrier is positioned on land belonging to the boundary but has no specific purpose, there is no downfall.
errors.why: The contrast is between a case that needs no carrier standing within the boundary (no offence) and one where such a carrier is used (sthūlātyaya), not the carrier's 'purpose'.

note: The customs-evasion casuistry and its sthūlātyaya rulings are mostly correct; two clauses are misconstrued.
A faithful rendering of the sūtra passage on the causes and conditions of defilement and purification and on the Tathāgata's samāpattis.

errors.english: it is impossible for them to possess number, because those two [note: collection and number] are entities of quality
errors.why: The 'two' are number (saṅkhyā) and conjunction (saṃyoga, ldan pa), both Vaiśeṣika qualities residing only in substances; 'collection' is not a quality.

note: The regress argument against space's distinct nature and the six padārthas is followed well; one gloss misidentifies the two qualities.

errors.english: Because one says "the one having a rabbit" [note: an epithet for the moon],
errors.why: The reason is 'because it is called moon'; 'the hare-marked' is the subject, not the reason.

fix.find: Because one says "the one having a rabbit" [note: an epithet for the moon],

errors.english: because they are not perceived in any way whatsoever
errors.why: ji ltar yang renders the Jaina kathaṃcit, 'in some respect'; the examples argue that things are non-existent or existent in some respect, not absolutely.

note: The verses on anyathānupapatti and reasons with a single characteristic are rendered soundly, apart from the moon example and the sense of kathaṃcit.

errors.english: By these words, the lord of men
errors.why: This completes ma bkur pa des, 'by that disrespect' (from the nāgas, Skt. avamānena), not 'by these words'.

note: Both the Sanskrit and the Tibetan verses are rendered faithfully, apart from the opening referent.

errors.english: the *Sub-commentary on the Requests* [note: original: "Zhu ba" / Vinayaupayika]
errors.why: zhu ba is the Vinaya 'Questions' (Vinayapṛcchā, in the Uttaragrantha), the canonical source text, not a sub-commentary or the Vinayaupayika.

fix.find: the *Sub-commentary on the Requests* [note: original: "Zhu ba" / Vinayaupayika]

errors.english: If it is covered with **planks**, there is no downfall.
errors.why: spang leb is turf or sod; it is shing leb (the next item) that means wooden planks.

errors.english: [note: the person responsible for the action leading to a transgression]
errors.why: Here the 'maker' (byed pa po) is the factor that constitutes the offence, i.e. the vihāra, as the answer shows, not a person.

errors.english: it is understood that the monastery is currently under the authority of the household
errors.why: The text says the rule covers every vihāra because no qualification such as 'owned by a householder' is stated; it does not assert that the monastery is under the household.

note: The pātayantika on building beyond three courses is broadly followed, but the source title, the roofing materials and the 'maker' gloss are wrong.

errors.english: Then because it has been abandoned, no bad reputation arises.
errors.why: The Tibetan says ill repute arises for him (he is shunned), like moonlight fading at dawn; the negation is added.

fix.find: Then because it has been abandoned, no bad reputation arises.
fix.replace: Then, because he is shunned, ill repute arises for him.

errors.english: even while I was being shaken, I did not let it go
errors.why: It is the anger that was stirring which he did not let loose, not he who was shaken (the same in the king's verse 'While you were being shaken').

note: A readable rendering of the dialogue on anger, but it inverts the fate of the angry man and misreads 'stirring' as applying to the speaker.
